task: Independent review of protocol error fixture dispatch/readiness measurement repair

findings.problem: Initial helper left preparation connect, controlled configuration_guard acquisition and disconnect outside the dispatch deadline; they could await the same admission lock without a local bound.
findings.resolution: Final helper separately bounds each of these three awaits to 3 seconds. The existing 3-second dispatch barrier and 3-second connectionRemoved wait remain, and the post-dispatch response timeout stays 300 milliseconds. This is not a single 3-second whole-test deadline.

checks.name: scope
checks.detail: Diff only changes a module registered under cfg(test). No production protocol/control implementation change in this repair.

checks.name: actual dispatch barrier
checks.detail: Peer writes and closes its requested marker before waiting on test-owned release. The test requires both that marker and outgoing session/new diagnostic within 3 seconds, and rejects early completion.

checks.name: response classification assertions preserved or strengthened
checks.detail: Original three actions and final session_requested assertion remain. Every incoming version-1 record still excludes error=protocol and protocolErrorClass/responseIdNull/beforeInitializeAccepted fields. Timeout must be outer Elapsed after dispatch and peer waiting marker; decode/EOF must be actual Ok(Err), not a caller timeout.

checks.name: controlled admission regression
checks.detail: New test acquires the real same-agent configuration_guard, polls open_session while holding it across 300 milliseconds, asserts no peer request receipt, then releases it and requires actual dispatch and decode failure. It preserves production Agent id/guard behavior.

checks.name: resource ownership and local wait bounds
checks.detail: Fixture has its own temporary directory/store/manager. Explicit disconnect is bounded and must succeed; connectionRemoved diagnostic is awaited with existing bounded until helper. Fixture Drop retains stop_for_shutdown fallback. The peer release wait belongs to the exact fixture process; no global cleanup or real Agent is introduced.

checks.name: additional clippy failure attribution
checks.detail: Optional clippy --tests failed on installed_initialize_probe.rs:78 and pty.rs:729. Both files currently have no HEAD diff. Required clippy succeeded. This review does not label the optional test-target lint check passed.

boundaries: The original whole-suite failure did not preserve its per-fixture trace. Controlled guard reproduction proves the old measurement premise was unsound, not the unique historical scheduling cause of that failure.
Review did not repeat tests, whole-suite checks, builds or installation; final combined integration remains root-owned.
Explicit async waits in this revised helper are separately bounded; this is not a hard real-time bound on filesystem operations or the complete test module.
Controlled Python peers establish test behavior only; no real Agent, authentication, installed-product or user-value acceptance follows from these results.
